html:
SMTO-RST-0018 — Another copy of SMTO is already using this data

GUID: 963450f7-46eb-5b44-95d4-b123be13978c
Slug: controller-owner-conflict
Domain: RST · Subsystem: controller

What happened

  • SMTO didn't start because another SMTO server is already using the same data folder, and only one can use it at a time. Your data hasn't been changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the startup screen shows Auto Fix: stop the other copy and start, select it and confirm. Auto Fix finds the other copy, lets it save its work, stops it, and then starts this one.
  2. Otherwise stop the other copy yourself: quit the installed SMTO app, or close any other window running ./startup.sh. Then select Start again. The data folder stays locked while the other copy runs, so this one can't start until it stops.
  3. If no other copy seems to be running, wait a minute, then select Start again. A copy that is shutting down keeps the data folder locked until it finishes saving.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen reaches Ready and your conversations appear.

If it still fails

  • Open Technical details, select Copy error details, and send them to the person who installed SMTO; they name the locked folder. Don't delete the lock file or anything else in the data folder while another copy might be running.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Server could not take the exclusive OS lock on owner.lock in its state directory, because another process holds it or the lock file is a symbolic link or not a regular file.

What this means

  • State ownership finds a symlink/nonregular lock target or cannot acquire the exclusive OS lock for the selected state directory. State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.

Why this can happen

  • State ownership finds a symlink/nonregular lock target or cannot acquire the exclusive OS lock for the selected state directory.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish unsafe lock-path shape from another live owner and inspect the actual lock holder.

How to fix it

  • Find the process holding owner.lock in the reported state root (normally under AOR_AGENT_STATE_DIR; the holder's PID and epoch are written in the file) and stop it normally so it saves its work; run only one HTTP worker per state directory. If the lock is reported as a symbolic link or not a regular file, replace it with a regular file only after confirming no Server is running; never remove a live owner's lock.
  • Use one Server worker for this state directory. Stop the previous owner normally and check the reported lock path; do not remove a live owner lock.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • One supported server owner holds a safe regular ownership fence without deleting another live lock.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
